_comment: All language-specific content lives in files like this one. bridge/coach.py, bridge/server.py and the prompt templates contain no words from any language. To add a language: copy this file, translate the content, then deploy with -c language=<filename without .json>.
_localeComment: BCP-47 codes for Amazon Transcribe, which gives the coaching lane an independent transcript and identifies which language was actually spoken. Streaming identification needs at least two options, one dialect each.
_espeakComment: espeak-ng voice used to phonemise the transcript into EXPECTED phonemes. It must match the language being taught: phonemising English text with the Spanish voice turns "Hello" into "e ʎ o", which makes the comparison against what Wav2Vec2 actually heard meaningless.
_voiceComment: Voices for es-US: lupe (feminine), carlos (masculine). tiffany and matthew are polyglot and also speak Spanish.
_genderComment: Must match the voice: gendered languages conjugate self-reference. Feminine voices: tiffany, amy, olivia, kiara, ambre, beatrice, tina, lupe, carolina. Masculine: matthew, arjun, florian, lorenzo, lennart, carlos, leo.
_regionalComment: Accent features the coach must never flag as errors. Getting this list right per language is what stops the tutor 'correcting' a native-sounding regional accent.
regionalVariation: "ll" or "y" pronounced as sh, zh, j, y or a palatal l (rioplatense and others) — all of these are correct, a plain English l is not
"c" or "z" as s instead of th (all of Latin America)
_learnerErrorsComment: The other side of the coin from regionalVariation: mistakes learners genuinely make that must NOT be excused as accent. Without these the reviewer treats almost everything as dialect and stays silent.
learnerErrors: pronouncing the silent "h" (hola, hombre) — it is always silent, and voicing it is an error rather than an accent
reading "ll" as an English plain "l" (tortilla as "tortila") — "ll" is a y-like sound, or a palatal l in some regions, but never a plain l
using English vowel qualities instead of the five pure vowels, or reducing unstressed vowels to a schwa
reading "j" or "g" before e/i as an English "j" instead of a throaty h
stressing the wrong syllable when it changes the word (esta / está, papa / papá)
_exampleComment: Shows the coach the house style for a note: plain language, no phonetic symbols, give the fix.
pronunciationExample: your 'rr' in 'perro' came out as a single tap, so it sounded like 'pero' (but)
grammarExample: 'yo comí' — for 'I ate' the -í ending already carries the yo
